haiku-low.q1: The 02:00 UTC scheduler starts it. It extracts orders with updated_at after W minus 2 h, up to the replica clock at snapshot start, including soft-deleted rows.
haiku-low.q2: Bulk imports hold transactions open up to 90 min, and updated_at is stamped at write time, not commit. So a row can appear on the replica up to 90 min after its updated_at.
haiku-low.q3: Every app write bumps updated_at. The next night's extract picks up the changed row again, and the conditional MERGE replaces the older version in fact_orders.
haiku-low.q4: The app sets deleted_at. The next night extracts it and the MERGE sets is_deleted = true on that row. No row is ever removed from fact_orders.
haiku-low.q5: The failed attempt commits nothing to fact_orders or W and is marked failed. It retries after 15 min, up to three attempts a night. After the third failure, on-call is paged.
haiku-low.q6: Dashboards keep showing the last committed fact_orders. A staleness alert is posted to the #data-alerts channel.
haiku-low.q7: The next Sunday reconciliation finds the mismatch on the order's creation day and reloads that whole day.
haiku-low.q8: The conditional MERGE on order_id inserts if no match, updates only if the staged updated_at is newer, and skips otherwise. So each order_id keeps exactly one row.
haiku-low.q9: In etl_watermark, one row holding W, the upper bound of the last successful attempt. W is written in Step 5's single transaction, committed with the MERGE.
haiku-low.q10: Step 5 is one warehouse transaction that commits the MERGE, the W update and the succeeded run status together. Dashboards see all of a night's changes or none.
haiku-low.q11: The failed attempt's staged rows are discarded, since the next attempt truncates stg_orders. It reads the same W, takes a fresh upper bound and re-extracts from W minus 2 h.
haiku-low.q12: It re-reads every order created on a mismatched day, applied via the same conditional MERGE in its own transaction. It does not move W, so the nightly high-water mark is unchanged.

sonnet.q1: The scheduler starts it at 02:00 UTC. It extracts orders with updated_at after lower (W minus 2 h) up to upper (replica clock at snapshot start), in one read snapshot, including soft-deleted ones (is_deleted = deleted_at not null).
sonnet.q2: Bulk imports hold transactions open for up to 90 min, and updated_at is stamped at write time, not commit. So the row can appear on the replica up to 90 min after its updated_at.
sonnet.q3: Every app write bumps updated_at, so the next night's extract picks up the changed row again, and the MERGE updates fact_orders because the staged updated_at is newer.
sonnet.q4: Deletes are soft: the app sets deleted_at (a write that bumps updated_at). The next night extracts it with is_deleted = true and the MERGE updates the fact_orders row. No row is ever removed from fact_orders.
sonnet.q5: Nothing is committed to fact_orders or W. The etl_runs row is marked failed. If fewer than 3 attempts tonight, wait 15 min and retry; after the third failure, on-call is paged.
sonnet.q6: Dashboards keep showing the last committed fact_orders. A staleness alert is posted to #data-alerts (data-alerts channel) by the 06:00 deadline check when there is no succeeded etl_runs row for tonight.
sonnet.q7: The next Sunday reconciliation: it finds the mismatch on the order's creation day (within the last 30 days) and reloads that day.
sonnet.q8: The MERGE on order_id is conditional: no match inserts; match with staged updated_at newer updates; match with not newer is skipped. So older or duplicate copies are skipped.
sonnet.q9: In the warehouse table etl_watermark (one row holding W). It is set to upper (the extract upper bound of that attempt), inside the Step 5 transaction together with the MERGE, committed at the same time.
sonnet.q10: Step 5 is a single warehouse transaction (MERGE, set W, mark run succeeded, COMMIT), so dashboards, which read only fact_orders, see all of tonight's changes or none. They never read stg_orders.
sonnet.q11: The next attempt truncates stg_orders (emptying the staged data), reads the same W, uses lower = W minus 2 h again, takes a fresh upper bound, and re-extracts.
sonnet.q12: It truncates stg_orders, then re-extracts every order created on a mismatched day. It applies them with the same conditional MERGE in its own transaction. W is not changed.
